access.note: A historical marker says the tower is open to the public during daylight hours. Current status not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: 132 wooden steps to the top room; the marker says the tower is open during daylight hours.

events.note: Sand Lake refuge established as a breeding area for migratory birds; CCC work on the refuge runs 1935 to 1939.
Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps; the marker gives 1936.

corrections.why: The marker, refuge brochure and magazine give 108 feet (about 32.9 m). The record's 30.5 m (100 ft) comes from one listing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The westlookouts listing says 100 feet; the marker, the refuge brochure and the magazine say 108 feet. The record is unchanged pending review.

The marker says the CCC camp ran 1925 to 1939; the brochure dates CCC work on the refuge to 1935 to 1939; the magazine ties the camp's work to the 1935 refuge designation. The story uses 1935 for the CCC work and 1936 for the tower.

sources.title: Sand Lake NWR Wildlife Drive brochure

notes_for_editor: The 1936 build date comes from the marker alone. The height is disputed (100 ft listing vs 108 ft in three sources); a correction to 32.9 m is proposed for review. The CCC camp dates conflict (marker 1925 to 1939 vs brochure 1935 to 1939). A 2025 federal solicitation for fire tower rehabilitation appeared in search results, but its page is behind a Cloudflare check and was not read, so it is not used; it may bear on current condition. Current access is unconfirmed; the marker's daylight-hours statement may be out of date. The tower is not tied to the headquarters building. Another Sand Lake tower (NWR 2) is listed as gone in the FFLA state list and is not this lookout.
